entries.problem: PR #556 remained red across repeated runs because orchestration stopped at workflow/job failure summaries instead of retrieving the available job logs; once logs were inspected, three reviewed-export routing tests were shown to use intentionally partial promotion-marker fixtures that the new EOF note-gap validator correctly rejected as invalid production authority.
entries.root_cause: Two coupled process defects: (1) CI triage did not descend workflow -> failed job -> job logs before declaring evidence unavailable; (2) narrow routing tests used a partial reviewed-authority fixture and mocked only the exporter consumer, so a newly added independent validator consumed the same marker and changed the fixture's meaning.
entries.correction: Retrieve failed job logs before any opaque-blocker classification. Keep production fail-closed behavior intact. In tests intentionally using partial authority fixtures, explicitly stub unrelated authority consumers so the test remains scoped to its owned behavior.
regression_protection: tests/test_authoring_export_reviewed_routing.py now isolates the EOF note-gap advisory in the three partial-authority routing tests
production project_note_gap_rule_findings remains fail-closed for stale/corrupt promoted authority
entries.verification: Fresh CI required on exact head 70e3f0c5de2657b79906f94db995d530f1df55bf; prior failure traceback confirmed identical three routing-test failures on Linux/Windows.
entries.residual_risk: Future validators may consume shared partial-authority fixtures in unrelated unit tests unless those tests explicitly declare/stub non-owned consumers.
entries.prevention_rule: For FAILED CI, always fetch actual failed job logs when the connector exposes them. For partial/mock authority fixtures, identify every consumer introduced by the change and either construct complete authority or explicitly isolate unrelated consumers; never weaken production validation to satisfy a narrow unit test.
